neighbours.label: the sentence boundary in expository science or history prose, right after a sentence that names a substance, object or process the next sentence will explain, as against the same boundary in narrative or casual everyday text
fire: Iron is carried around the body by haemoglobin. Haemoglobin is a protein found in red blood cells.
Archaeologists found a bronze mirror in the tomb. Mirrors like this were made by polishing metal.
Caffeine blocks receptors for adenosine in the brain. Adenosine normally makes us feel sleepy.
The comet's tail is made of gas and dust. Because the tail points away from the sun, it changes direction.
Plants store energy as starch in their roots. Starch is a long chain of glucose molecules.
Lead pipes were common in Roman cities. Lead is toxic and slowly damages the nervous system.
The reaction is slowed down by cold temperatures. In winter, therefore, the process takes longer.
Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called polyps. Polyps take calcium from sea water.
quiet: Tom put his keys on the table by the door. Then he went upstairs to change.
We found a cheap mirror at the market on Saturday. Mum hung it in the hall.
I had two coffees before the meeting this morning. Now I can't sit still.
The dog ran out into the garden after the ball. Then it rolled in the mud.
My aunt keeps potatoes in a sack in her shed. She cooks them every Sunday.
Sam fixed the old pipes in our bathroom last week. He charged us forty pounds.
It was cold when we left the house this morning. Lucy forgot her gloves again.
Ana went swimming at the reef with her cousins. They stayed until sunset.
